content: Tomato Early Blight symptoms: Dark brown to black concentric ring spots on older leaves first. Spots enlarge and may cause yellowing and defoliation. Stem and fruit lesions possible. Caused by Alternaria solani.
Tomato Early Blight treatment: Apply Mancozeb (75% WP) at 2.5g/L or Chlorothalonil (75% WP) at 2g/L. Alternate with Azoxystrobin (23% SC) at 1ml/L. Apply at 7-10 day intervals during wet weather.

Tomato Late Blight symptoms: Water-soaked, greenish-dark lesions on leaves. White fuzzy growth on leaf undersides in humid conditions. Rapid plant death in severe infections. Caused by Phytophthora infestans.
Tomato Late Blight treatment: Apply Metalaxyl + Mancozeb (Ridomil Gold) at 2.5g/L or Fosetyl Aluminum (80% WP) at 2.5g/L. Remove and destroy infected plants immediately. Spray before rain events.
Tomato Leaf Curl (TYLCV) symptoms: Upward curling and cupping of leaves. Yellowing of leaf margins. Stunted growth. Reduced fruit set. Transmitted by whitefly (Bemisia tabaci).

Tomato Leaf Curl treatment: No direct cure for viral infection. Control whitefly vector using Imidacloprid (17.8% SL) at 0.3ml/L or Thiamethoxam (25% WG) at 0.3g/L. Remove infected plants. Use reflective mulches to repel whiteflies.
